requirement:
A paragraph has no declared name. Each prose paragraph has an anonymous
`paragraph` node under its nearest
enclosing outline container. This includes paragraphs before the first heading
and inside list items, quotations, and directive bodies. Their selectors follow
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`. Heading text and literal
code-block contents create no paragraph nodes. Syntax that has no outline node
is transparent when finding the enclosing container.
rationale:
The three `{test}`-marked tests in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/markdown_tests.rs` cover each obligation in `requirements.sdk.sources.markdown.paragraphs`.

- **Anonymous `paragraph` node under the nearest enclosing container.**
  - `fn[paragraphs_and_nested_directives_have_independent_source_ranges]` asserts the full `kinds(&outline)` list. It shows paragraphs parented to the section, to the outer `block` and to the inner nested `block`. A paragraph that closes a nested directive returns to the correct parent.
  - The same test checks that every node's selector resolves back to its index and that anonymous segments have the form `paragraph@<12 chars>`.
- **Paragraphs before the first heading, in list items, in quotations and in directive bodies.**
  - `fn[paragraphs_in_transparent_lists_and_quotes_are_selectable]` uses a source with a pre-heading paragraph, a list paragraph, a quoted paragraph and a post-heading paragraph under a setext heading. It asserts exactly 4 paragraphs at lines [1, 3, 5, 10].
  - It asserts that the first three share the same enclosing container and that the last is parented to `section[Title]`. This covers transparency of the list and quote syntax, which has no outline node.
  - Directive bodies are covered by the nested `note` and `tip` cases in the first test and in `fn[anonymous_identities_survive_reflow_and_sibling_edits_and_number_duplicates]`.
- **Heading text creates no paragraph.**
  - The exact node list in the first test has no paragraph for `# Authentication`.
  - The exact count of 4 in the second test rules out a paragraph for the setext `Title` heading.
- **Literal code-block contents create no paragraph.** The first test's trailing ```` ```text ```` fence yields only a `block` node, with no paragraph child, in the exact node list.
- **Selectors follow `requirements.references.outline_selectors`.**
  - `outline.resolve(&node.selector)` round-trips for every node.
  - The `#1` and `#2` suffixes for duplicate paragraphs are asserted in `fn[anonymous_identities_survive_reflow_and_sibling_edits_and_number_duplicates]`.
  - That test also checks that selectors stay stable under reflow and sibling edits.

Other, unmarked tests in the file also assert that literal or unfinished fences produce no paragraph nodes. This is supporting evidence only, and it does not change the verdict.

I found no untested obligation or weak assertion. Indented code blocks and paragraphs in lists nested inside directives are not tested separately. The requirement does not single them out, and they go through the same container and transparency logic that the tests already exercise.
